The MPFC model used in this study includes an inertial term for the atomic density field, allowing it to capture fast propagation of the solidification front.
The study investigated the growth of the (100), (110), and (111) faces of a BCC crystal lattice invading a homogeneous liquid.
The sequence of growth velocities observed was V(100) > V(111) > V(110), which agrees with the Bravais law of crystallography.
The growth anisotropy, defined as the ratio V(100)/V(110), was around 1.29 at low driving forces and decreased towards 1 as the driving force increased.
Increasing the relaxation time τ led to a nonlinear decrease in the front velocities for all the BCC faces.
At high driving forces ε and relaxation times τ, the MPFC model predicted the formation of disordered crystal structures near the solidification front.
The systematic error in the determination of front velocities was estimated to be around 4.2%.
The computational domain used in the simulations was a slab with periodic boundary conditions along the elongated sides and isolation on the other surfaces.
The position of the solid-liquid interface was determined by the minimum of the time derivative of the atomic density field, corresponding to the highest gradients of the chemical potential.
The velocity scale V0 used in the dimensionless results was calculated from the scales of front position, time, and material parameters.
The free energy functional of the MPFC model includes terms for the atomic density field, atomic flux, and their interactions.
The MPFC model utilizes a one-mode approximation with r0 = 0 and q0 = 1, corresponding to a stable BCC structure.
The equilibrium lattice parameter and initial average density were determined from the free energy minimization.
The numerical simulations were performed using a finite element method with Lagrange-C2 elements in a three-dimensional computational domain.
The hyperbolic term in the MPFC equation was proposed to incorporate both mass diffusion and fast elastic relaxation.
